text: Some time later, Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David fell in love with her.

versions.text: Some time later, this happened. Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David fell in love with her.
versions.explanation: "Some time later, this happened." is a redundant, choppy rendering of the Hebrew narrative formula וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי־כֵן. Dropping the empty second clause keeps the sense and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Amnon was so tormented over his sister Tamar that he made himself ill, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible to him to do anything to her.
Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
He said to him, "Why are you, the king's son, so haggard morning after morning? Won't you tell me?" Amnon answered, "I am in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."

Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare the food where I can see it, so that I may watch and eat from her hand.'"

So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes here in front of me, so that I may eat from her hand."
David sent word to Tamar at the palace: "Go to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare food for him."
So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, where he lay in bed. She took dough, kneaded it, shaped the cakes in his sight, and baked them.
Then she took the pan and served him, but he refused to eat. "Send everyone out of here," Amnon said, and they all left him.
Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the bedroom.
But when she brought them to him to eat, he seized her and said, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
"No, my brother!" she said. "Do not violate me. Such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not commit this outrage.
And I—where could I carry my disgrace? And you would be like one of the depraved fools in Israel. Speak to the king; he will not keep me from you."
But he would not listen to her, and being stronger than she was, he overpowered her and raped her.
Then Amnon was seized with a violent hatred for her; the hatred he felt for her was greater than the love he had felt. "Get up and get out!" he said to her.
"No," she said, "sending me away is a greater wrong than what you have already done to me." But he would not listen to her.
He called the young man who served him and said, "Get this woman out of my sight, and bolt the door behind her."
She was wearing an ornamented robe, for this is how the virgin daughters of the king were dressed. So his servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the ornamented robe she was wearing, laid her hand on her head, and went away, crying aloud as she went.

Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, my sister, keep quiet. He is your brother; do not take this thing to heart." So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.

versions.text: Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? For now, my sister, keep quiet. He is your brother; do not take this thing to heart." So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.
versions.explanation: "For now" suggests a temporary silence, which is not in the Hebrew; וְעַתָּה is the ordinary transitional "but now / and now."

text: When King David heard all about it, he was furious.
But Absalom said nothing to Amnon, good or bad; he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar.
Two years later, when Absalom's sheepshearers were at Baal Hazor near Ephraim, Absalom invited all the king's sons.
Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant is shearing sheep. Will the king and his servants please come with your servant?"

versions.text: Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant has sheepshearers. Will the king and his officials please come with your servant?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew repeats עֶבֶד ("servant") deliberately—"his servants ... your servant"; rendering the first as "officials" loses the wordplay. Also "Your servant is shearing sheep" is closer to הִנֵּה־נָא גֹזְזִים לְעַבְדֶּךָ than "has sheepshearers."

text: "No, my son," the king replied. "We should not all go; we would only be a burden to you." Although Absalom pressed him, he still refused to go, but he gave him his blessing.
Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon come with us." "Why should he go with you?" the king asked.
But Absalom pressed him, so he sent Amnon along with all the king's sons.

Absalom ordered his men, "Watch closely. When Amnon is in high spirits from the wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon down,' then kill him. Have no fear. Have I not given you the order myself? Be strong and courageous."
So Absalom's men did to Amnon exactly as Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's sons got up, each mounted his mule, and fled.
While they were still on the way, this report reached David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons; not one of them is left."
The king stood up, tore his garments, and lay down on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "My lord must not think that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons. Only Amnon is dead. This has been Absalom's fixed purpose from the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
So now, let my lord the king not take it to heart, thinking that all the king's sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."
Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man on watch looked up, he saw many people coming along the road behind him, on the side of the hill.

versions.text: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man on watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road on the western side of the hill.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "from the road behind him, from the side of the hill." The rendering "western" reflects an ancient version rather than the Hebrew text, and the phrase "behind him" (אַחֲרָיו) has been dropped. If the alternate reading is retained, it should be marked in a footnote.

text: Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the king's sons have come. It has happened just as your servant said."
As he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived, weeping loudly. And the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
Absalom, however, had fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. And the king mourned for his son day after day.
After Absalom had fled to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
And King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon's death.
